I think it would be beneficial to cull from the api a top list of users based on submission/comment points as a way to encourage further activity on the site.
Public list of users with top submission/comment points

Argument for: people love useless points and to make numbers go up that's why places show post counts, join dates and karma so it would further encourage submission especially to new folks who wanted to make a name for themselves. At this point anything that encourages submissions should be looked at.

Argument against: karma and imaginary internet points are literally why we can't have nice things. People will spam garbage which will further draw in "that crowd" whom will spam more garbage that will be upvoted and puns will ensue, call it redditism if you like and quality posting takes much more effort so it will always get drowned out and upvoted less, possibly discourage quality contributors. If you wanted to keep content fresh and quality you'd need strict moderation and lots of rules limiting and deleting many submissions.

I don't know man and I'm glad I'm not an admin to have to make this call, I can see pros and cons in either so I guess my vote would be "don't do it" since the downsides to doing it could potentially have the worst outcome for us over the long term. That's a "soft vote" though and I could be persuaded either way with a good argument.

As much as this would be helpful for common factors, I don't think it will be as beneficial for having a rank list of non-related numbers. Now have an adjustment where you could filter through the sites data, that would be better to implement. This way the community has an open policy that allows for people to see stats from as little s a verses highlights, to as large as ordered lists of submitter in a certain time span. The more open ended, the better it is to offer data in the way one wishes to see it

I would imagine a protocol that would utilize the current search engine by categorizing data based on content submission, then being split into link posts, discussion posts, and comment posts - with the users being linked to their contribution (as this can also be paired with the current up/down vote ratios used in profiles)

The idea for the top ordered karama & submissions is not the best way to organize & assess data - it may offer a piece of a larger puzzle, but ultimately I would aim to revise the concept to allow community interaction with the data. With the stats of just postings or karma, you are limited to take it for face value when there are dozen free will reasons someones could have taken to actually submit certain content, or offer their vote. It is better to work towards a balanced system, even if it is something that hasnt been implemented on a site such as reddit (especially since reddit is heading into a direction that focuses on face value & not intellectual understanding)

I think this would actually be a great thing to implement on a per-community basis. The categories should cover rankings for volume of submissions, volume of comments, score of each, and voting on each.

This could actually help with the monetization model that WhoaVerse is considering because it would encourage awareness of top contributors in a way that would make those gaming the system more likely to be caught. Once urbane, this could force those who game the site to optimize effectiveness with account age because making many short-lived accounts would avoid the leader boards while sacrificing notoriety.
